Aircraft Structure.name: Aluminum
Aircraft Structure.reasoning: Primary structural metal used extensively for aircraft frames due to its high strength-to-weight ratio and corrosion resistance; absolutely essential in modern UAV structures.

Aircraft Structure.name: Titanium
Aircraft Structure.reasoning: Used in critical load-bearing areas of aircraft structure for its strength and corrosion resistance; standard in aerospace applications though costly compared to aluminum.

Aircraft Structure.name: Carbon
Aircraft Structure.reasoning: Used in carbon fiber composites which provide high strength and low weight; common in advanced UAV structures although not universal, some designs opt for metal only.

Aircraft Structure.name: Epoxy resins
Aircraft Structure.reasoning: Essential as a binder matrix in composite structures like carbon fiber; commonly used but other resins exist, so moderately confident.

Aircraft Structure.name: Glass
Aircraft Structure.reasoning: Material for certain composite reinforcements or transparent parts (canopies), used variably so less critical than metals and carbon composites.

Aircraft Engine.name: Titanium
Aircraft Engine.reasoning: Used in turbine blades and other high-stress engine parts for its high strength, temperature resistance, and corrosion resistance; very commonly used in aircraft engines.

Aircraft Engine.name: Nickel
Aircraft Engine.reasoning: A key component in high-temperature nickel-based superalloys forming turbine blades and combustion sections, essential for engine operation.

Aircraft Engine.name: Aluminum
Aircraft Engine.reasoning: Used in some engine components, especially in auxiliary systems and housings due to lightweight; common but alternatives exist.

Aircraft Engine.name: Copper
Aircraft Engine.reasoning: Used in electrical wiring and cooling systems within the engine, widely used though alternatives exist.

Aircraft Engine.name: Steel Ingots
Aircraft Engine.reasoning: Materials like stainless steel are used for shafts and other structural parts within the engine; relatively standard though alloy types vary.

Landing Gear.name: Steel Ingots
Landing Gear.reasoning: Primary material for landing gear struts and structural parts due to high strength and toughness; absolutely essential in most designs.

Landing Gear.name: Titanium
Landing Gear.reasoning: Used for weight reduction in some high-end UAV landing gear components; less common but a standard aerospace material.

Landing Gear.name: Aluminum
Landing Gear.reasoning: Used in non-critical landing gear components and housings to save weight; common alternative but not always used.
